verses: Then Jesus went home, and once again a crowd gathered, so that He and His disciples could not even eat.
When His family heard about this, they went out to take custody of Him, saying, “He is out of His mind.”
And the scribes who had come down from Jerusalem were saying, “He is possessed by Beelzebul,” and, “By the prince of the demons He drives out demons.”
So Jesus called them together and began to speak to them in parables: “How can Satan drive out Satan?
If a kingdom is divided against itself, it cannot stand.
If a house is divided against itself, it cannot stand.
And if Satan is divided and rises against himself, he cannot stand; his end has come.
Indeed, no one can enter a strong man’s house to steal his possessions unless he first ties up the strong man. Then he can plunder his house.
Truly I tell you, the sons of men will be forgiven all sins and blasphemies, as many as they utter.
But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will never be forgiven; he is guilty of eternal sin.”
Jesus made this statement because they were saying, “He has an unclean spirit.”
Then Jesus’ mother and brothers came and stood outside. They sent someone in to summon Him,
and a crowd was sitting around Him. “Look,” He was told, “Your mother and brothers are outside, asking for You.”
But Jesus replied, “Who are My mother and My brothers?”
Looking at those seated in a circle around Him, He said, “Here are My mother and My brothers!
For whoever does the will of God is My brother and sister and mother.”
title: Who Are My Family
season_line: Jesus has just named His twelve on the mountain, and now He comes home to a packed house, a worried family, and accusers from Jerusalem.
big_idea: Jesus is stronger than every power that binds us, and He makes everyone who follows Him part of His own family.
frame: Home is where we most want to be understood, and sometimes it's where faith feels strangest. Jesus knew that: His own family thought He'd lost His mind. Yet He didn't stop loving them. Over time His mother and brothers came into His circle ({{Acts 1:14|Acts 1:14}}). He also opened a wider family: everyone who sits at His feet and does God's will. So your household is not a private castle. It is one room in God's big house, built by the One who tied up the strong man to set captives free. Carry two things into today: patience with relatives who don't yet see it, and an open door for those who need family.

carry.text: For whoever does the will of God is My brother and sister and mother.”

glance.head: Family Thinks He's Lost It
glance.line: The crowds are so heavy that Jesus can't eat, and His family comes to take Him home, saying He's out of His mind.

glance.head: The Strong Man Bound
glance.line: Scribes say His power is from Satan; Jesus shows that's absurd, says He has come to tie up the strong man, and warns against calling the Spirit's work evil.

glance.head: A New Family Circle
glance.line: When His mother and brothers call for Him, Jesus points to those sitting around Him and says whoever does God's will is His family.

understand: Mark loves to tell stories like a sandwich. He starts with Jesus' family coming to grab Him (v. 21), slips in the scribes' accusation (vv. 22-30), then returns to the family at the door (vv. 31-35). The two halves explain each other. Family and religious experts both misread Jesus. One group says He's crazy, the other says He's demonic. Yesterday we saw Jesus call twelve ordinary people to be with Him. Today we see who is really with Him and who is standing outside.

The scribes can't deny the healings, so they credit them to Beelzebul, a name for Satan. Jesus answers with plain logic: a house fighting itself falls. Then He tells a short parable. To rob a strong man, you first tie him up. Satan is the strong man, and the people he holds are his goods. Jesus is the stronger One John promised ({{Mark 1:7|Mark 1:7}}), come to bind the enemy and set the captives free. Every demon driven out is proof. This echoes God's promise to rescue captives from the mighty ({{Isaiah 49:24-25|Isaiah 49:24–25}}).

Verses 28-29 have worried many tender hearts. Notice first how wide the mercy is: all sins and blasphemies can be forgiven. The one sin that can't be forgiven is what the scribes were doing (v. 30). They looked straight at the Spirit's saving work and called it evil, refusing the only One who forgives. It's a settled, hardened rejection, not a slip of the tongue. If you are worried you've done it, that worry is itself a sign your heart is still soft toward God.

Jesus' words about His mother and brothers sound sharp, but He isn't rejecting them. Later He cares for His mother from the cross ({{John 19:26-27|John 19:26–27}}), and His brother James became a believer and leader ({{1 Corinthians 15:7|1 Corinthians 15:7}}). He is redefining family around Himself. The people sitting in a circle around Him, listening, are as close as blood. That's the family God has been building since He promised Abraham a family of many nations.

word.gloss: Greek for strong or mighty. John the Baptist used a form of it for Jesus, the One 'more powerful' coming after him, so Mark is quietly saying the stronger One has arrived to overpower the strong man.

glow: he first ties up the strong man
Here are My mother and My brothers!
whoever does the will of God

god.short: Pray by name for a relative who finds your faith strange.
god.full: Pray by name for one relative who thinks your faith is odd or too much. Ask Jesus, the stronger One, to loosen whatever holds them, and to make you patient and kind toward them.
god.why: Jesus' own brothers didn't believe at first, yet later they joined the praying disciples ({{Acts 1:14|Acts 1:14}}).

together.short: Tell each other one way you saw the other do God's will.
together.full: Before you part, take thirty seconds each to tell the other one specific way you've seen them do God's will lately. You're spouses, and in Jesus' words, you're also brother and sister.

others.short: Invite someone without family nearby to a meal or Thanksgiving.
others.full: Think of someone at church or work who has no family close by, a student, a widow, or someone far from home. Text them today with an invitation to a meal, maybe even your Thanksgiving table.
others.why: Jesus' family is everyone sitting around Him doing God's will ({{Mark 3:34-35|Mark 3:34–35}}).

tonight: Where has following Jesus felt misunderstood in our families, and how can we love them well without letting that steer us?

more.line: Jesus' own brothers didn't believe in Him yet.
His mother and brothers later praying with the disciples.
God promises to free captives from the mighty.
